## NativeBodyOptions interface

How a body shapes the records it returns.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface NativeBodyOptions
```

[absentValueMarkers?](./core.nativebodyoptions.absentvaluemarkers.md)

</td><td>

`readonly`

</td><td>

boolean

</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Hand the codec the value of each property whose evidence makes the app's "no such object" failure its empty value marked as such, so the codec takes that failure, raised while it reads the value's identity, as `null` (<!-- -->).

Only a body whose result the codec encodes by a typed plan wants this. Under a passthrough plan the codec returns the result unchanged, so a marker would reach the caller as it is. A failed read of such a property is `null` either way. Defaults to `true`<!-- -->.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[containerReferences?](./core.nativebodyoptions.containerreferences.md)

</td><td>

`readonly`

</td><td>

boolean

</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Hand the codec each reference whose target is got within the record being read together with that record, so the codec encodes the reference with the record as its container (phases/13 D7, container scoping). A get, create, update or resolution body hands over the item it read; a list body, the row's identifier it already read.

Only a body whose result the codec encodes by a typed plan wants this. Under a passthrough plan the codec converts nothing, so the hand-over would reach the caller as it is. Defaults to `true`<!-- -->.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[identifierAliases?](./core.nativebodyoptions.identifieraliases.md)

</td><td>

`readonly`

</td><td>

boolean

</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Add the legacy identifier aliases to list items: the identifier value under the stable key `id`<!-- -->, and, when a resource is matched on a working property instead of its declared identifier, that property's value mirrored into the declared identifier field.

Only operations whose output passes through unconverted want these: their callers pass `item.id` back as the `id` request parameter. A typed output contract declares its record fields exactly and derives references from the record itself. Its encode silently drops undeclared keys such as `id`<!-- -->, but a mirrored identifier field is declared, so encode would accept it holding another property's value. A typed body must therefore produce only the declared fields, each holding its own value. Defaults to `false`<!-- -->.

</td></tr>

_(Optional)_ Build a list body that reads one page window, given as the body's third argument, and returns a page window result, instead of reading the whole collection into an array (see `PageWindow` and `PageWindowResult`<!-- -->). Meaningful only for a list command of a resource with an identifier. Defaults to `false`<!-- -->.
